paragraphs.en: The train door opened, and the smell hit me before my feet touched the platform. Salt, wet wood, and something sweet from the kiosk. Eight years, and Harrow Bay still smelled exactly the same.
paragraphs.zh: 车门打开，还没等下到站台，那股气味就扑面而来。咸味、湿木头味，还有小卖亭飘来的甜味。八年了，哈罗湾的气味一点没变。

paragraphs.en:
"You're standing in the doorway," said a voice behind me.

"I'm having a moment," I said.

"Have it on the platform."
paragraphs.zh:
“你堵在门口了。”身后有人说。

“我在感受这一刻。”我说。

“去站台上感受。”

paragraphs.en: I stepped out. The station was small, as I remembered. One line along the sea, a wooden roof, a bench with peeling paint. I had a suitcase, a school bag, and no clear plan for the year. I wanted quiet. I wanted to keep my head down and finish second year without any turbulence.
paragraphs.zh: 我走出去。车站很小，和我记忆中一样。沿海一条线，木屋顶，一张掉漆的长椅。我拎着行李箱、背着书包，对这一年没什么明确计划。我想要安静，想低着头、平平稳稳地念完二年级，不要有任何波折。

paragraphs.en: The kiosk beside the ticket gate was still there. It was a small wooden stand with a glass case of snacks, a shelf of maps, and a hand-written sign that said OPEN. Behind it sat a girl in a Northlight High uniform, drawing in a sketchbook. She did not look up.
paragraphs.zh: 检票口旁的小卖亭还在。那是个木头小摊，玻璃柜里放着零食，架子上摆着地图，还有一块手写的牌子，写着“营业”。亭子后面坐着一个穿北光高中校服的女孩，正在速写本上画画。她没抬头。

paragraphs.en:
"Excuse me," I said. "Is the bus stop still on the left?"

"Right," she said, still drawing.

I looked right. There was the bus stop.

"Thanks."

"Mm."
paragraphs.zh:
“打扰一下，”我说，“公交站还在左边吗？”

“右边。”她说，还在画。

我往右看。公交站就在那儿。

“谢谢。”

“嗯。”

paragraphs.en: The bus climbed the slope toward school, and I pressed my forehead to the window. Lantern Street passed below, shutters half open, a bakery with a warm light in its window. My heart did something awkward and sudden, and I looked away.
paragraphs.zh: 公交车沿着斜坡往学校开，我把额头贴在车窗上。灯笼街从下面经过，卷帘门半开着，有家面包店的窗里透出暖光。我的心突然别扭地跳了一下，我移开了视线。

paragraphs.en: The first day of second year is always a mess. New class lists, new seats, new rules nobody explains. I found Class 2-B on the second floor and walked in. A boy with a wide grin grabbed my shoulder before I even sat down.
paragraphs.zh: 二年级的第一天总是乱糟糟的。新的分班名单、新的座位、没人解释的新规矩。我在二楼找到2-B班，走了进去。我还没坐下，一个咧嘴笑的大个子男孩就一把抓住了我的肩膀。

paragraphs.en: "New guy!" he said. "Park. Theo Park. I know everything about this town and nothing about you, which is a problem I plan to fix." He talked like a congress of one, all motion and no pause. "You came from the city? Big city? Did it have, like, real buildings?"
paragraphs.zh: “新来的！”他说，“帕克。西奥·帕克。这镇上的事我全知道，你的事我一点不知道，我打算解决这个问题。”他说话像一个人开的议会，一刻不停。 “你从城里来的？大城市？有真正的高楼吗？”

paragraphs.en:
"It had buildings," I said. "Some of them were big."

Theo nodded with great seriousness. "I can work with that."
paragraphs.zh:
“有楼，”我说，“有的还挺高。”

西奥一脸严肃地点点头。“行，这个信息有用。”

paragraphs.en: Ms. Hale read the class list in a flat voice and assigned committee work to anyone who sighed too loudly. She also asked for a student to help the council sort old files after school. Nobody raised a hand. Then the door opened and someone answered for me.
paragraphs.zh: 黑尔老师用平板的声音念分班名单，谁叹气太大声就派谁去做委员会的工作。她还问有谁愿意放学后帮学生会整理旧文件。没人举手。这时门开了，有人替我回答了。

paragraphs.en:
"Elliot Reed will do it," said a girl with dark hair and a perfect ribbon. She said my name like she had checked it against a list. "He needs to learn the school. I'll supervise."

"I don't remember agreeing," I said.

"You hesitated," she said. "That's close enough."
paragraphs.zh:
“埃利奥特·里德会去。”一个深色头发、系着完美丝带的女孩说。她说我名字的样子，像刚从名单上核对过。“他需要熟悉学校。我来监督。”

“我不记得自己答应过。”我说。

“你犹豫了，”她说，“差不多了。”

paragraphs.en: Her name was Vivian Ashe. Student council secretary, top of the year, and clearly someone who enjoyed watching people tangle themselves up in their own words. I could tell she had a strong sense of her own prominence, and a weakness for using it.
paragraphs.zh: 她叫薇薇安·阿什。学生会书记，年级第一，显然还喜欢看别人被自己的话绕进去。我看得出她对自己挺有优越感，也爱把这份优越感拿出来用。

paragraphs.en: After the last bell, I went to the council office. Vivian handed me a box of old papers without a word. Sorting them was boring, but the window was open and the sea was right there, so I didn't mind.
paragraphs.zh: 最后一节课的铃响后，我去了学生会办公室。薇薇安一句话不说，递给我一箱旧文件。整理这些很无聊，但窗户开着，海就在眼前，我倒不介意。

paragraphs.en:
On my way out, an old woman stopped me near the library. She was small and bent, and she held a brown parcel with both hands. "You're the Reed boy," she said. "You have your mother's eyes. This was left for you. It says to give it to you when you come back."

"When I come back?" I said. "I only moved away."

She just smiled and put it in my hands.
paragraphs.zh:
出来的时候，一位老太太在图书馆附近叫住我。她个子矮小，背有点弯，双手捧着一个棕色包裹。“你是里德家的男孩，”她说，“你有你妈妈的眼睛。这是留给你的。上头写着等你回来的时候交给你。”

“等我回来？”我说，“我只是搬走了而已。”

她只是笑了笑，把包裹放进我手里。

paragraphs.en: Inside was a small leather notebook. It was water-stained and soft at the corners, palm-sized, and clearly old. Inside the cover someone had drawn a map of the town by hand. I opened the first page at the bus stop.
paragraphs.zh: 里面是一个小小的皮面笔记本。水渍斑斑，边角都软了，巴掌大小，显然很旧。封皮内侧有人手绘了一张镇子的地图。我在公交站翻开第一页。

paragraphs.en:
The handwriting was childish and neat. Seven pages. Seven promises. The first one said: I promise to eat Nora's cooking for a week and say it is good every single time. — E.

I turned the page. The seventh page was sealed with old tape, and written on the front in a voice I could almost hear: To the girl who waited at the station.
paragraphs.zh:
字迹幼稚却工整。七页纸，七个约定。第一个写着：我承诺吃诺拉做的饭整整一星期，而且每次都说好吃。——E。

我翻到下一页。第七页用旧胶带封着，封面上写着一句我仿佛能听见的话：给在车站等的那个人。

paragraphs.en: Nora. The bakery on Lantern Street. The girl in my old class who once pushed me into the sea and then cried about it. I sat on the bench and read the page again, letters wavering and people moving around me, and for the first time in eight years I felt something I could not put into a well-labeled genre.
paragraphs.zh: 诺拉。灯笼街那家面包店。我旧班上的那个女孩，曾经把我推进海里，然后又为此哭了。我坐在长椅上又读了一遍那页，字迹在眼前晃动，周围有人在走动。八年来第一次，我感到一种我说不清、归不了类的情绪。

paragraphs.en:
The bench creaked. Someone sat down beside me, very close, and then a hot paper bag was put into my hands.

"You're back," Nora said. "You're really back. I didn't believe it when the bakery got the delivery address. Eat. You look like a weed that survived winter."
paragraphs.zh:
长椅吱呀一声。有人在我旁边坐下，靠得很近，然后把一个热乎乎的纸袋塞进我手里。

“你回来了。”诺拉说，“你真的回来了。面包店收到送货地址时我还不信。吃。你看起来像一棵熬过冬天的杂草。”

paragraphs.en: She was loud. Even her silence was loud. Her name was written clearly on the first page of the notebook, and she was watching me open the bag with the defense of someone who had rehearsed this and was still scared.
paragraphs.zh: 她声音很大。连沉默都很大声。笔记本第一页上清清楚楚写着她的名字，而她看我打开纸袋时，那副样子像是在防守，像一个排练过很多遍却仍然很紧张的人。

paragraphs.en:
"Nora," I said. "Do you remember a notebook? A promise notebook?"

Her face went through several expressions quickly, then settled on a wide, determined grin. "Nope," she said, in the voice of a person who absolutely did.
paragraphs.zh:
“诺拉，”我说，“你记得一个笔记本吗？一个写约定的笔记本？”

她脸上飞快地闪过好几种表情，最后定格成一个大大的、坚决的笑容。“不记得。”她说，用的却是那种“绝对记得”的语气。

paragraphs.en:
"You're a terrible liar."

"I'm a great liar," she said. "You just have a chronic habit of seeing through me. Eat the bread, El."
paragraphs.zh:
“你撒谎撒得很糟。”

“我撒谎撒得很好，”她说，“你只是有看穿我的老毛病。吃面包吧，埃尔。”

paragraphs.en: I ate the bread. It was good, because it came from her parents, not from her. I appraised the notebook again while she watched me from the corner of her eye. Then she took the last bun, gave it to me, and ran for the train she did not need to catch.
paragraphs.zh: 我吃了面包。面包很好吃，因为她父母做的，不是她做的。她斜着眼看我的时候，我又仔细看了看那个笔记本。然后她拿走最后一个面包，塞给我，然后跑去赶那趟她根本不用赶的火车。

paragraphs.en: On the ride home, a sea wind came through the window and rumpled the pages. I turned them over and counted: one, two, three, four, five, six. And a sealed seventh. Under the map inside the cover, there was one more line, small and pressed into the paper: We don't break these. We don't forget.
paragraphs.zh: 回家的车上，海风从窗里灌进来，把书页吹得翻动。我把它们翻过来数：一、二、三、四、五、六。还有一个封着的第七页。封皮内侧的地图下面，还有一行小字，压进了纸里：这些我们不撕毁，也不忘记。

paragraphs.en: The bus turned along the seawall. The old Annex building stood dark behind the school, and its clock had stopped at 4:10. I had seen it a hundred times as a child. That night it looked like a question someone had left for me, and I had just promised myself a quiet year.
paragraphs.zh: 公交车沿着海堤转弯。学校后面，旧别馆黑沉沉地立着，上面的钟停在4:10。小时候我见过它一百次。那晚它看起来像有人留给我的一道问题，而我刚刚还对自己保证要过安静的一年。

paragraphs.en:
At home, my sister Iris was waiting at the door. She is fourteen, sharp, and keeps a notebook of her own, though hers is called a suspicious behavior log and I am the main entry.

"You're late," she said. "What's in the bag?"

"Homework," I said.

"Homework doesn't have a ribbon."
paragraphs.zh:
回到家，妹妹艾里斯在门口等着。她十四岁，很精明，也有一个笔记本，不过她那本叫“可疑行为记录”，而我常常是主要条目。

“你回来晚了。”她说，“袋子里是什么？”

“作业。”我说。

“作业不会系丝带。”

paragraphs.en: I hid the notebook under a book on my desk. Before bed I opened the seventh page one last time under my lamp. The tape was old. The paper underneath was too new, and the handwriting was not quite mine. I turned off the light and stared at the dark ceiling, and the small voices inside me would not settle.
paragraphs.zh: 我把笔记本藏在桌上的书下面。睡前，我在台灯下最后看了一次第七页。胶带很旧，可下面的纸太新了，笔迹也不太像我的。我关了灯，盯着黑黑的天花板，心里的那些小声音怎么也平静不下来。

paragraphs.en: My phone lit up. An unknown number. One line: You opened it, didn't you. I'll tell you the rules tomorrow. Don't do anything stupid before then.
paragraphs.zh: 手机亮了。一个陌生号码。只有一行字：你翻开了，对吧。明天我告诉你规则。在那之前别干傻事。

paragraphs.en: I lay there in the dark, and outside, a train passed along the sea and did not stop.
paragraphs.zh: 我躺在黑暗里。外面，一列火车沿着海开过去，没有停。
